pull.title: KAFKA-21374: Prevent cross-thread header leakage in global state stores
pull.body:
Summary
This PR addresses KAFKA-21374, where global state store reads can receive incorrect record headers from the global processing thread.
While investigating the issue, I found that the global processor context retains headers from the record being processed. Since the same context is used by the global state store, other threads can receive unrelated headers during serialization and deserialization.
This can cause problems for applications that depend on record headers for deserialization.

Changes Made
* Updated GlobalProcessorContextImpl to allow the owning global thread to access its record headers, while returning empty contextual headers for reads from other threads.
* Updated GlobalStateUpdateTask to clear the record context after processing, including when an exception occurs.
* Added regression tests to cover header leakage during normal processing and concurrent global store reads.
* Added tests to verify thread ownership and record context cleanup.

Testing
I first reproduced the issue with a failing regression test and confirmed that the deserializer was receiving headers from an unrelated global record.
After applying the fix, I ran the relevant Kafka Streams tests.
* 323 selected tests passed.
* Sequential and concurrent regression tests passed.
* Both at-least-once and exactly-once test scenarios passed.
* Checkstyle passed.
* Spotless passed.
* SpotBugs passed.
* git diff --check passed.
The concurrent scenario was tested using TopologyTestDriver with controlled thread synchronization. I have not run a separate real-broker concurrency integration test.

JIRA: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21374
Reviewers: Alieh Saeedi <asaeedi@confluent.io>

reviews.body: Thanks @srv9989 for the fix! The approach looks right to me. Clearing the record context in update() fixes the leak between records, and the thread check fixes the race for stream-thread and IQ reads. Just few things before merging. Please check the comments.

review_comments.body: Clearing the context here breaks direct writes to a global store from TTD after a record was piped. For example, `put` on a cached `globalTable` store NPEs in `CachingKeyValueStore.putInternal` (`recordContext().headers()`), and tombstones on headers stores fail the same way. TTD already sets a dummy context for task stores in `getStateStore()` when none exists. Can you do the same for the global context and add a test?

`GlobalStateManagerImpl.reprocessState()` also sets the record context for each restored record and never clears it, so store access in processors' `init()` still gets the last restored record's headers. Clear it there too?

This assumes the context is built on the thread that later calls `update()`. That holds for `GlobalStreamThread`, but in TTD it's the thread that builds the driver, so a test that pipes from another thread (e.g. `assertTimeoutPreemptively`) silently gets empty headers on the global processor's own writes too. Please document this assumption here.
This passes on trunk too, since the test record has empty headers, and the `assertNull` above already covers it. Drop it?
